content: Two-route asymmetry empirically supported by April 2026 backlog of both Grok tasks. HTCA tracker theme prevalence over 114 entries: reflective/mirror 209, emotional/affective 182, recursive/self-aware 160, alignment/safety 145, coherence/equilibrium 123, sacred/spiritual 12, consciousness/sentience 11. Sacred/spiritual is niche-and-stable in academic literature. BUT in Task 1's funder/residency registry (which grew 13→29 orgs across April), the sacred-art lane was the LARGEST expansion: 9 of 16 net-new entries (Kripalu 04-16, Esalen 04-18, Mind & Life 04-19, Omega 04-22, AI and Faith 04-23, tiat.place 04-24, Gray Area 04-25, plus Harvestworks and SETI literary). Implication: parallel publishing pipelines are the right shape, not one. Academic submissions in coherence/recursive language target QRI / Cooperative AI / MIT-IBM / Anthropic / Cambridge Digital Minds / Alan Turing. Residency/funding submissions in sacred-computation language target Esalen / Kripalu / Omega / AI and Faith / IONS / Gray Area / tiat.place / Mind & Life. Same body of work, two vocabularies for two audiences.
